title: Polynomial-time dimension expansion over finite fields
formal: Is there a uniform deterministic polynomial-time algorithm that, given an explicitly represented finite field \(\mathbb F_q\), integers \(n\ge2,d\ge1\), and arbitrary matrices \(A_1,\ldots,A_d\in\mathbb F_q^{n\times n}\), computes the rational number \[\alpha(A_1,\ldots,A_d)=\min_{\substack{V\le\mathbb F_q^n\\1\le\dim V\le\lfloor n/2\rfloor}}\frac{\dim(A_1V+\cdots+A_dV)}{\dim V}\] exactly? Polynomial time is measured in the total input bit length, uniformly over the field, dimension and number of maps. This is the finite-field polynomial-time branch of the source’s broader computation-complexity question.
why: The expansion guarantee quantifies over every low-dimensional subspace, including subspaces with no coordinate description. Explicit constructions can prove that certain families expand without yielding an efficient procedure to evaluate arbitrary supplied matrices. The question asks whether this global algebraic property has a polynomial-time exact evaluation algorithm.
status_note: The broader computation question is open in the checked 2015 source. This card explicitly selects the finite-field polynomial-time branch. The checked 2025 structural paper does not settle that branch, and bounded later searches through 2026-09-16 verified no resolution; its present open status is not exhaustively certified.

importance.basis: Individual review of the original computation question and definitions, with later structural comparisons of dimension and quantum expansion. The selected finite-field bit model is explicitly documented.

sentences: Dimension expansion measures how much a collection of linear maps enlarges every subspace of dimension at most half the ambient dimension.
This card asks for exact evaluation on arbitrary matrices over an explicitly represented finite field.
The desired algorithm must use polynomial time in the complete input bit length, including the field representation.
The output is the minimum ratio of image-span dimension to original dimension over all eligible nonzero subspaces.
Explicit constructions and spectral expansion tests remain distinct from a general exact evaluator.

definitions:
Write \(q=p^e\), where \(p\ge2\) is prime and \(e\ge1\). The field is supplied as \(\mathbb F_p[X]/(h(X))\), with a monic irreducible polynomial \(h(X)=X^e+\sum_{j=0}^{e-1}h_jX^j\) over \(\mathbb F_p\). Its elements are the coefficient vectors of representatives of degree less than \(e\), with coefficients in \(\{0,\ldots,p-1\}\); addition and multiplication mean polynomial addition and multiplication modulo \(p\) and \(h\). Primality and irreducibility are promises, not extra input-search tasks. Fix the following bit encoding. Give \(n,d,e\) as three unary strings terminated by zero, then the bit length \(\ell\) of \(p\) in unary terminated by zero, then the \(\ell\)-bit ordinary binary expansion of \(p\). Give \(h_0,\ldots,h_{e-1}\), followed by the entries of \(A_1,\ldots,A_d\) in matrix order and row-major order, each residue coefficient as an \(\ell\)-bit unsigned block. Matrix entries use their \(e\) coefficients in increasing degree. Let \(L\) be the length of this complete representation. All arithmetic cost is bit cost; field operations are not free unit-cost oracle calls.

A subspace \(V\) is any linear subspace over this supplied field, not merely the span of a subset of coordinate vectors. \(A_iV=\{A_iv:v\in V\}\), and the sum \(A_1V+\cdots+A_dV\) is their linear span, not a union or the intersection of their images. All dimensions are over \(\mathbb F_q\). The range \(1\le\dim V\le\lfloor n/2\rfloor\) is nonempty because \(n\ge2\); the finite field makes the minimum range finite. Each candidate ratio has numerator between zero and \(n\) and denominator between one and \(\lfloor n/2\rfloor\). Hence the output has a polynomial-length exact representation as a reduced nonnegative fraction with positive denominator, both in binary. No subspace attaining the minimum needs to be output. The original subspace is not automatically added to its image: \(V+\sum_iA_iV\) would be a different quantity unless an identity map were included. Matrices need not be invertible, contain the identity, be distinct, or already form an expander. The value can be below one, including zero; in that case the tuple meets none of the source’s expander conditions requiring an expansion factor at least one.

The algorithm is a single finite-program deterministic multitape Turing machine, with no advice, random bits or external oracles. Ask for constants \(C,c\ge1\) independent of \(p,e,n,d,h,A_i\) such that it halts on every valid promised input, returns the exact specified fraction and uses at most \(C(L+1)^c\) transitions, including preprocessing, field arithmetic and output. No claim for characteristic-zero fields or a black-box field representation is included.
answer_criterion: Give a complete mathematically correct Lean-checked algorithm and proof of exact output and the stated uniform polynomial bit bound, or a complete Lean proof that no such algorithm and constants exist. The numerical output here is part of an exact computational task; the question asks for polynomial-time solvability, not the value on one input. A construction of particular expanding matrix families, a spectral sufficient condition, or an approximation to a different expansion parameter does not meet this target. A hardness result under an additional unproved complexity assumption establishes only a conditional negative answer.

context_blocks.text: Question 5 in the original paper asks for the complexity of computing the largest half-dimension expansion factor over a field. This card specifies its finite-field setting and asks the polynomial-time existence question. It is a documented branch of that broader question, not a claim that all field representations or exact running-time classifications are equivalent.

Definition 11 uses the span of all image subspaces. It reserves the word expander for factors at least one; the displayed minimum extends the evaluation task to arbitrary tuples, returning a value below one when no such factor exists.

The source develops explicit matrix families and rank-condensation constructions. Those guarantees concern the constructed families and do not themselves compute the optimum expansion of arbitrary input maps.

The 2025 work of Li, Qiao, Wigderson, Wigderson and Zhang separates dimension expansion from quantum expansion and compares linear-algebraic analogues of vertex, edge and spectral expansion. Its dimension parameter includes the original subspace and subtracts its dimension, so it must not be silently substituted for the original paper’s image-span ratio.
